You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — KapStone (post-merger, within WestRock) realized record, ~3-5-year horizon (~2021-2023)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. KapStone itself deregistered shortly after
> closing; the acquirer (WestRock Company, CIK 1732845) continued reporting and its
> subsequent Form 10-Ks are used here strictly for facts that separately name the
> acquired business or a specific legacy-KapStone asset. This sub-dossier contains no
> information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On November 15, 2018, KapStone Paper and Packaging Corporation filed a Form 15-12B
  certifying termination of registration of its common stock under Section 12(g) of the
  Exchange Act, recording approximately 1 holder of record as of the certification date.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001171843-18-007975, Form 15-12B]
- No further periodic reports (10-K/10-Q) were filed by KapStone as a standalone
  registrant after this deregistration. [SRC: SEC accession 0001171843-18-007975, Form 15-12B]
- WestRock's subsequent Form 10-Ks state that KapStone's financial results have been
  included in WestRock's Corrugated Packaging reportable segment "since the date of the
  acquisition" — combined with pre-existing WestRock assets rather than reported as a
  standalone acquired business. [SRC: SEC accession 0001564590-21-057778, Form 10-K FY2021]
- WestRock's Exhibit 21 list of "Significant Subsidiaries" as of September 30, 2021 does
  not include an entity named "KapStone Paper and Packaging Corporation"; the filing does
  not state whether this reflects a subsequent renaming, merger-out, or the entity simply
  falling below the "significant" disclosure threshold. [SRC: SEC accession 0001564590-21-057778, Form 10-K FY2021, Exhibit 21] [UNVERIFIED: reason for omission]

## Documented facility-level event tied to a specific legacy-KapStone asset
- KapStone's own Form 10-K for fiscal 2017 identifies a containerboard mill in North
  Charleston, South Carolina as one of its four containerboard mills (acquired from
  MeadWestvaco Corporation in 2008), staffed by approximately 560 employees. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-18-001015, Form 10-K FY2017]
- WestRock's Form 10-K for fiscal 2019 (the first full fiscal year after the merger)
  disclosed plans to "reconfigure" its North Charleston, SC mill beginning in fiscal
  2020, reducing linerboard capacity by approximately 288,000 tons and annual costs by
  approximately $40 million, including a multi-month workforce reduction. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-19-011534, Form 10-K FY2019]
- WestRock's Form 10-K for fiscal 2023 states that during fiscal 2023 the company
  "recorded various impairments and other charges associated with our decision to
  permanently cease operations at our Tacoma, WA and North Charleston, SC containerboard
  mills," which "ceased production in September 2023 and June 2023, respectively." [SRC: SEC accession 0000950170-23-064855, Form 10-K FY2023]

## Segment-level financial record (not KapStone-specific)
- WestRock's Form 10-K for fiscal 2023 reports a pre-tax, non-cash goodwill impairment
  of $1.9 billion recorded in the second quarter of fiscal 2023, allocated $1.4 billion
  to the Global Paper reportable segment and $0.5 billion to the Corrugated Packaging
  reportable segment (the segment that includes former KapStone operations alongside
  pre-existing WestRock assets); the filing states this segment-level impairment
  "materially adversely affected" fiscal 2023 operating results. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950170-23-064855, Form 10-K FY2023]
- No source was located in which WestRock discloses a standalone net income, revenue, or
  comparable financial scalar attributable specifically to the former KapStone business
  (as distinct from the combined Corrugated Packaging segment) for the ~2021-2023
  window. [UNVERIFIED]

## Items sought but not found
- No reputable-press or primary source was located specifically attributing the fiscal
  2023 North Charleston, SC mill closure decision to KapStone-origin performance, to
  culture/organizational friction, or to any other named cause distinct from WestRock's
  general portfolio-restructuring rationale (redirecting capital "to improve other key
  assets"). [SRC: SEC accession 0000950170-23-064855, Form 10-K FY2023] [UNVERIFIED: causal attribution]
- No divestiture, bankruptcy, or dissolution of the acquired KapStone business (as
  opposed to a single facility) was found disclosed within the ~2021-2023 window.
  [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- KapStone deregistered as a public reporting company on November 15, 2018 and filed no
  further standalone periodic reports; its financial results were folded into WestRock's
  combined Corrugated Packaging segment with no separate segment-level disclosure, so no
  standalone financial-performance scalar for the acquired business is publicly available
  for the ~2021-2023 window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001171843-18-007975, Form 15-12B] [SRC: SEC accession 0001564590-21-057778, Form 10-K FY2021]
- One specific, dated, documented event ties to a named legacy-KapStone asset within the
  fixed window: the North Charleston, SC containerboard mill — one of KapStone's four
  mills at the time of the 2018 transaction, already flagged for capacity reconfiguration
  in WestRock's first post-merger annual report — permanently ceased production in June
  2023, with associated impairment and restructuring charges recorded at the WestRock
  segment level. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-19-011534, Form 10-K FY2019] [SRC: SEC accession 0000950170-23-064855, Form 10-K FY2023]
- Per the no-record convention, the standalone financial outcome of the acquired business
  is coded **uncertain**: WestRock discloses only combined segment results and one
  named-facility discontinuation event, not a separately attributable financial
  trajectory for the specific business acquired in 2018.

[SLICE END]
